question: For series combination the correct relation between R, R₁, R₂ is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**R = R1 + R2**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When resistors are connected in series, they are connected one after the other, so that the current flows through each resistor in turn.
 
• The equivalent resistance of the circuit is the sum of the individual resistances. 
 
• **Why is R = R1 + R2?**
 
 
• Imagine a series circuit with two resistors, R1 and R2.
 
• The current flowing through both resistors is the same.
 
• The voltage drop across each resistor is proportional to its resistance (V = IR). 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• The total voltage drop across the circuit is the sum of the voltage drops across each resistor.
 
• Therefore, the total resistance of the circuit is the sum of the individual resistances.
